help.open_work_q: How do I open a set of papers?
help.open_work_a1: Download the class’s submissions from your school’s system as a ZIP, then open the assignment on the class’s Course line and press **Bring papers in**, or drop the ZIP on it. A folder, loose PDFs, Word files and photos work the same way.
help.open_work_a2: **Bring papers in** also opens a folder, a scan of the whole class, or files to match to a roster.
help.open_work_a3: The papers are kept in this browser, so the set is waiting on Home and in To do the next time you open the app.

help.try_sample_q: Can I try it without real papers?
help.try_sample_a1: Yes. **Try the sample class** in Settings, Display opens two made-up classes part-way through a term, with marked papers, a gradebook, a timetable and lessons. Type “sample” in Find anything to get there.
help.try_sample_a2: The sample is kept apart from your own work. **Leave the sample** in Settings, Display clears it in one click, and your own work is as you left it.
help.find_anything_a1: One box that reaches every student, assignment, tool, setting and help answer. Open it from the top of the sidebar, or press **Ctrl K** (**⌘K** on a Mac).
help.find_anything_a2: Type a few letters of what you want, move with the arrow keys and press Enter. Each row does the same thing as the button for it.
help.find_anything_w: search command palette ctrl k shortcut
help.full_screen_q: Can the app fill the whole screen?
help.full_screen_a1: Yes. Press **F**, or turn on **Full screen** in Settings, Display. While a paper is open the button is in the top bar, beside ✕. The browser’s bars go away and the sidebar folds to icons. On the marking screen the sidebar goes away too, so the paper gets the room.
help.full_screen_a2: Press **F** again, the same button, or **Esc** to leave. Nothing is closed or lost on the way in or out. On formative work F is for feedback, so use the button there. Lessons and Present work the same way.
help.full_screen_a3: While a paper is open, the student list hides as well: rest the pointer at the left edge of the screen, or press **[**, and it comes back. In **Settings, Marking** you can keep it shown, or hide the tools too.

help.add_class_q: How do I add a class and its roster?
help.add_class_a1: 1. Press **Add a class** in the sidebar and give it a name.
help.add_class_a2: 2. Paste the student names, one on a line. Students are kept in the order you paste them.
help.add_class_a3: 3. Open the class’s **People** tab to add an ID, an email or a note for each one.
help.add_class_a4: With a roster, every student is listed when you open papers for that class, including anyone who turned nothing in.

help.todo_q: How does the to-do list work?
help.todo_a1: **To do** in the sidebar is one list. Your own to-dos have a solid circle. Lines with a dashed circle are things the app noticed from your saved work: papers to mark, papers to hand back, a class with no lesson planned, missing work to chase.
help.todo_a2: Type a to-do the way you would say it and press Enter. A day at the end (“tomorrow”, “friday”, “nov 20”), a class name or a student’s name is picked out for you, and a click on what was understood takes it off. Press **N** anywhere outside a paper to add one.
help.todo_a3: Click a line to give it a day, a class, something it goes with, a repeat or a note. The app’s own lines go by themselves when the work is done. You can move one to another day, hide it, or switch a whole kind off. **People** names someone from your School page, with an Email link when their address is saved.
help.todo_a4: **Home** shows your own to-dos that are overdue or due today. The list is saved with your grading work, never in your Planner folder.

help.todo_week_q: Can I see my to-dos by week?
help.todo_week_a1: Yes. On **To do**, choose **Week** at the top right, or open Calendar, **By time**. The same lines sit on the days they are for, with a Later column for the rest.
help.todo_week_a2: Type in a day to add a to-do for it, and drag a line to another day. Anything not done by its day moves to today on its own, and says which day it was for.

help.focus_q: Is there a timer for grading in short sessions?
help.focus_a1: Yes. **Focus** in To do, the focus button on Home, or **Focus on this** on a to-do or a lesson starts a session in one press. Pick what to work on: a set of papers waiting to be marked, a lesson, or one of your to-dos. A set of papers opens at the next paper with no score. The timer sits in the bottom left corner of every screen. When the time is up, a soft chime plays and you can take a break, keep going, or stop.
help.focus_a2: Set a daily goal in papers or minutes in **Settings, Focus and goals**. A paper counts when its score is finished, wherever you do it. To do, Home and the timer show how far along you are, and turn green when you get there. The length of a session and a break, and the chime, are set there too.

help.time_tracker_q: Can I see how much time I spend grading and planning?
help.time_tracker_a1: Yes, in the **Time tracker**, from **Time this week** in To do, or Find anything. Grading time counts while the marking screen is in front. Planning time counts in a focus session on a lesson, and after a few minutes of steady work on lessons, the Calendar or a Course line, but not while you present or during your classes. It stops after a few idle minutes.
help.time_tracker_a2: The tracker shows a week, a month or three months: totals, a bar for each day, grading by assignment and planning by lesson. Use **Add time** for work done away from the app. **Download as a spreadsheet** saves it as a CSV file. **Settings, Focus and goals** has when counting stops, and how soon planning work counts.

help.plan_grading_q: Can the app tell me how long my grading will take?
help.plan_grading_a1: Yes, once you have finished a few papers with the time tracker on. Each set then shows about how long its papers will take at your pace: in the Focus box and the **Grading plan** in To do, and on the assignment’s card.
help.plan_grading_a2: The Focus box also offers a free period between your classes, picks up the set you were last on at the paper you left, and can start small with **3 papers**. On the day you choose, Home shows a look back at the week. Each can be switched off in **Settings, Focus and goals**.

help.session_goals_q: Can I set a goal for each focus session?
help.session_goals_a1: Yes. Before you start, pick one under **Goal for this session**: a few papers, the whole set, the to-do, or a few words of your own. The app suggests one from your pace, and the timer shows how far along you are.
help.session_goals_a2: When the session ends, you see if you reached it. A goal you didn’t reach goes into your next session on the same work, so a set can take a few sittings with breaks in between. **Don’t carry it over** lets it go.

help.school_resources_q: Where can I keep my school’s links and files?
help.school_resources_a1: On **School** in the sidebar. Keep the handbook, the calendar, the bell schedule, the portals you sign in to, forms, and notes like who to call. Put them in groups you name, and press the flag on the ones you open most to keep them at the top.
help.school_resources_a2: **Add**, then **Link**, when the school keeps it online, since a link stays up to date by itself. **Add**, then **File**, keeps a copy of a file with your work, up to 50 MB each. You can also drop files on the page or paste a web address.
help.school_resources_a3: Tick a class under **For a class** when a link, file or note belongs to one class. The page can then show one class at a time, and a link for a class shows on every lesson for that class, under **Links** and in **Present**, all year. A lesson’s own links go in that same **Links** box, typed or picked from here.
help.school_resources_a4: Everything is saved with the rest of your work: in this browser, in your folder and in a take-home file. Find anything finds each one by its name. **People** at the top has a spot for each role, like your principal. Fill in the ones you need, or use **Change the spots…** for your school’s own roles.

help.ib_myp_a3: 2. In the class’s **Grades** tab, every task shows the levels it gave. Click a level on the right to see all of a student’s evidence for a criterion and choose the level that fits best.
help.ib_myp_a4: 3. Once every criterion has a level, the total becomes the final grade of 1 to 7. Levels are never averaged for you. For a task marked on paper, use **+ Add levels** on the Grades tab.

help.ib_dp_a3: In the same box, **Components** sets how much each type of work counts in this class alone. On the Grades tab, **Predicted grades** opens a list where you click the grade you predict for each student. The grade the percent earns is outlined as a hint.

help.grading_way_q: My school grades with letters, percent or 1 to 7. Can I set that?
help.grading_way_a1: Yes. Settings, **Grading and scales** has how you grade: rubric rows, points, percent, letter grades, IB MYP criteria (0 to 8) or IB DP 1 to 7, with the boundaries for each letter or level.
help.grading_way_a2: It is your default for new assignments. Each assignment can still be set its own way in Rubric setup.
help.grading_way_w: letters A B C percent IB 7 boundaries bands default scale
help.status_q: How do I mark a paper missing, excused or late?
help.status_a1: Under the student’s total in the score panel, pick **Missing**, **Excused** or **Late**. The ⋯ beside them has **Leave out of the average**.
help.status_a2: Missing and excused papers have no score to wait for, so they don’t count as left to mark.
help.status_w: absent no paper exempt late status
help.extra_credit_q: How do I give extra credit?
help.extra_credit_a1: On one paper, open the ⋯ beside the score and choose **Extra credit points**. It takes points or a percent.
help.extra_credit_a2: For extra credit that is not tied to a paper, press **+ Extra credit** on the class’s **Grades** tab. Term setup says whether it adds to the term grade and whether a grade can pass 100%.
help.retake_q: A student is redoing an assignment. How do I keep the first score?
help.retake_a1: Open the ⋯ beside Missing, Excused and Late on their paper and choose **Start a retake**. The first try’s score, comment and paper are kept, and the score panel empties for the retake. Add the new paper with **+ Add**.
help.retake_a2: The highest try counts unless you choose the latest or the average: **Change** in the retake box, or Term setup on the Grades tab. It is one rule for all your classes.
help.retake_a3: For a score you typed on the Grades tab, type both into the cell, like **7 > 10**.
help.retake_w: retake resubmit resubmission redo second attempt try again rewrite highest latest average
help.past_work_q: Can I see a student’s earlier work while I mark?
help.past_work_a1: Yes. **Past work**, under Next in the score panel, shows the student’s scores and your comments from other assignments beside the paper on screen.
help.past_work_a2: Students are matched through the class roster.
help.return_q: How do I hand marked papers back?
help.return_a1: 1. Open the assignment’s **Return** tab. It first lists anything unfinished: scores not given, students with no paper.
help.return_a2: 2. Press the blue button. The app makes a ZIP with each student’s marked file in the same folders they came in, named like “Ana Lee - River essay - Graded.pdf” (Feedback when there is no score).
help.return_a3: 3. Upload that ZIP, or the files in it, to your school’s system.
help.return_a4: To hand back one paper straight away, use the **Export … paper now** button under Previous and Next.
help.return_w: export download return give back zip send students flatten
help.anchor_papers_q: How do I pick and export anchor papers?
help.anchor_papers_a1: Anchor papers are the high, middle and low paper your school keeps from a summative. While you mark, click **High**, **Mid** or **Low** under the score. Each level belongs to one paper, so picking another paper moves it.
help.anchor_papers_a2: The **Return** tab lists the three. **Export anchor papers** downloads them in one ZIP, each named for the assignment and its level, like “Persuasive essay - Summative High.pdf”.
help.anchor_papers_a3: Student names are covered the same way as for an AI assistant: typed names and your own cover boxes are blacked out. A handwritten name needs a box, so use **Check the covers** on the card first. Untick **Cover student names** to export them as they are.
help.anchor_papers_w: anchor exemplar high mid middle low moderation standard sample papers
help.feedback_page_q: What is the feedback page on a returned paper?
help.feedback_page_a1: Each returned paper starts with a page for the student: the score, each rubric row with the level you gave and what it means, your comment, and every comment on the paper with its page number.
help.feedback_page_a2: It is on unless you turn it off under **Options** on the Return tab. Your own pages are not changed.
help.feedback_page_w: cover summary first page student sees report
help.copy_grades_q: How do I get scores into my school’s gradebook?
help.copy_grades_a1: Open the assignment’s **Grades** tab. Every student is listed with row scores, total, percent and your comment. Click any cell to copy it, then paste it into your school’s system.
help.copy_grades_a2: The order can be the folder order or your roster order, whichever matches the screen you are pasting into.
help.copy_grades_w: copy paste managebac canvas powerschool transfer enter marks
help.change_after_q: Can I change marks after I have exported?
help.change_after_a1: Yes. Your marks stay in the app, so open the assignment, change them and export again.
help.change_after_a2: With **Keep marks editable** ticked on the Return tab, each exported PDF also carries your marks. Opening that export on another computer brings them back as marks you can move or delete.
help.gradebook_a1: Open a class from the sidebar and choose its **Grades** tab. It has every assignment for the class in one table, grouped by type, with an average for each type and a term grade.
help.gradebook_a2: **+ Add scores** types in scores for work that was not marked here.
help.gradebook_a3: To type scores straight into the table, click a cell or start typing on it. **Enter** goes to the next student and **Tab** to the next assignment, and a column copied from a spreadsheet can be pasted onto the first cell.
help.gradebook_w: grades table term average overall marks book enter paste spreadsheet keyboard
help.import_scores_q: Can I bring in scores from my old gradebook?
help.import_scores_a1: Yes. In the class’s **Grades** tab press **Import…**, then choose a CSV or Excel file, or paste the cells from your spreadsheet. One row per student, one column per assignment.
help.import_scores_a2: Before anything is saved you see each column with its type, date and what it is out of, which rows matched your roster, and any score that is already on the Grades tab. Scores already there stay unless you choose the file’s.
help.import_scores_w: import csv excel xlsx spreadsheet sheets upload old gradebook switch mid-year past scores
help.google_classroom_q: Can I bring a class over from Google Classroom?
help.google_classroom_a1: Yes, with two downloads and no sign-in. In Settings, **Classes and terms**, press **From Google Classroom…**.
help.google_classroom_a2: First the grades file: in Classroom, open any assignment’s Student work page, click the gear and choose Download all grades as CSV. It brings the students, every assignment with its points and date, and the scores. You check the scores before anything is saved on the Grades tab.
help.google_classroom_a3: For the papers, open the Classroom folder in Google Drive, then the class, then the assignment’s folder, and download it. Bring that ZIP in on the assignment. Files named “Student name - title” are put together under each student. A file a student uploaded under its own name opens as its own entry for you to match.
help.google_classroom_a4: Both files are read in this browser and nothing is sent anywhere. Scores can’t be sent back into Google Classroom from here: the Grades tab lists them to copy across.
help.google_classroom_w: google classroom drive import bring move switch transfer csv grades roster students submissions folder zip connect sign in
help.terms_q: How do I set terms and how much each type counts?
help.terms_a1: Settings, **Classes and terms** has your terms and their dates, and what share of the term grade each type of assignment carries. Formative work never counts toward the grade.
help.terms_a2: An assignment counts toward the term its due date falls in.
help.terms_w: semester quarter weights percent summative formative weighting
help.types_q: Can I make my own assignment types, or change their order?
help.types_a1: Yes. Open **Term setup** from a class’s **Grades** tab or from Settings, **Classes and terms**. Under **Types, and what a grade is made of** you can rename a type, add your own with **+ Add a type** (Homework, Projects, Quizzes), and give each its share of the grade.
help.types_a2: The arrows beside each type set the order. That is the order of the gradebook’s columns from left to right, and of the choices wherever you pick a type.
help.types_a3: A type can be removed once no assignment is in it. Formative stays feedback only: a ✓ in place of a score.
help.types_w: category categories custom reorder order left right homework quiz project rename weights columns in-class summative
help.one_student_q: How do I see everything about one student?
help.one_student_a1: Open the class, choose **People** and click a name. The student’s page has every score, the term grade, and how they are moving.
help.one_student_a2: The **Charts** under the class’s **Grades** tab show the same numbers for everyone at once.
help.one_student_w: profile individual parent meeting conference progress chart
help.attendance_q: Can I take attendance in the app?
help.attendance_a1: Yes. Open a class, choose **People**, then **Attendance**. Everyone starts as present, so press **Late** or **Absent, reason unknown** only for a student who isn’t, or **Everyone is here** if they all are. Each press is saved, with a note if you want one.
help.attendance_a2: When you learn an absence is excused, open that day and press **Absent, excused**. **Look back** lists the absences that still have no reason.
help.attendance_a3: **Look back** shows every saved day in one table, with each student’s totals. **Copy this day** and **Download as a spreadsheet** take it out for your school’s system.
help.attendance_a4: Attendance stays in this browser and your folder, like the rest of your work. If you don’t use it, turn it off in Settings, **Classes and terms**.
help.attendance_w: attendance register roll call present absent absence late tardy excused unexcused unknown reason
help.learning_goals_q: Can I see scores by learning goal or standard?
help.learning_goals_a1: Yes, and it is optional. In Settings, Grading and scales, **Learning goals** holds your own list: a skill like “Uses evidence”, or a standard from your school.
help.learning_goals_a2: 1. In an assignment, choose Setup, then **Rubric setup**, and pick a goal beside each row. For a paper quiz, pick a goal under each question in **Quiz boxes**.
help.learning_goals_a3: 2. Open the class’s **Grades** tab and choose **Goals**: the class average on each goal with the lowest first, every student by every goal, and where each number came from.
help.learning_goals_a4: A student’s own page shows their goals beside the class average. Tagging never changes a score or a grade, and every assignment counts the same within a goal.
help.learning_goals_w: standards standard skills objectives outcomes mastery reteach tag strand competency
help.report_comments_q: Can it help me write report comments?
help.report_comments_a1: Yes. Open the class’s **Grades** tab and choose **Report comments**. Each student has a draft built from the term grade, the strongest and weakest rubric rows, missing work and how the scores have moved.
help.report_comments_a2: Change any of it, bring in what you wrote on their papers with **Add**, and press **Done, next student**. **Copy all** puts every comment on the clipboard for your report system.
help.report_comments_a3: No AI writes the drafts and nothing is sent anywhere. **Wording…** lets you rewrite the sentences they are built from.
help.report_comments_w: report card term comment end of term narrative parents
help.seating_q: Can I make a seating chart, groups, or pick a student at random?
help.seating_a1: Yes. Open a class, choose **People**, then **Seating**. Pick how the room is set up, then drag each student to a desk. Dropping one student on another swaps them.
help.seating_a2: **Shuffle** gives everyone a new seat, with Undo. Click a student and choose **Keep in this seat** for anyone who should not move. The **⋯** menu arranges the desks, shows the chart to the class and prints it.
help.seating_a3: **Pick a name** in the class header shows one student at random, and nobody twice until everyone has had a turn. **Make groups** deals the class into groups; drag a name to move it, or click two names to swap them. **Make my own** starts every group empty. **Who’s here** leaves out anyone away today. Ctrl Z takes back a move or a shuffle.
help.seating_a4: While presenting a lesson, press **P** to pick a name and **G** for groups. The names are only shown: they are never put in a lesson or in your Planner folder.
help.seating_w: seat seats desk desks seating plan chart shuffle random picker name cold call groups teams pairs partners wheel
help.missing_work_q: How do I remind students about missing work?
help.missing_work_a1: Open a class and choose its **To do** tab. It lists every paper you marked Missing, by student or by assignment, for the term you pick.
help.missing_work_a2: **Email reminder** opens an email in your own mail app, already addressed and listing what the student owes. Read it and send it yourself: The app sends nothing. **Email all** on an assignment writes one email with every address in Bcc.
help.missing_work_a3: Emails come from the People tab. **Email wording…** changes what every reminder says.
help.missing_work_w: late overdue not handed in owe chase nag email reminder parents
help.progress_sheet_q: Can I print a page about a student for a parent meeting?
help.progress_sheet_a1: Yes. Open the class, choose **People** and press **Progress sheets** for a page per student, or click a name and press **Progress sheet** for one.
help.progress_sheet_a2: Each page has the term grade, the average for each type, every score, a chart of how they moved, missing work, each term’s grade, the report comment and lines for notes. Choose the term at the top, and untick what you don’t want.
help.progress_sheet_a3: Press **Print** and choose a printer or Save as PDF. It is made on your computer and nothing is sent anywhere.
help.progress_sheet_w: conference parent teacher meeting print pdf progress report summary one page
help.where_saved_a1: In this browser, on this computer, as you work. There is no save button and no account.
help.where_saved_a2: A browser can be cleared, so choose a folder as a second copy: Settings, **Saving and sync**. Until then Settings says your work is only in this browser.
help.where_saved_a3: In Safari and Firefox, which cannot save to a folder, make a take-home file now and then.
help.where_saved_w: save backup folder storage lost cleared safe
help.other_computer_q: How do I move my work to another computer?
help.other_computer_a1: 1. In Settings, **Saving and sync**, press **Take my work with me**. It makes one file protected by a passphrase you choose.
help.other_computer_a2: 2. Carry the file to the other computer.
help.other_computer_a3: 3. There, press **Bring work in**. It shows what will change before anything does.
help.other_computer_a4: The trip back works the same way. If the same student changed in both places, you see both versions and choose. Your lessons go too. Lessons already on that computer stay, and only the ones it does not have come in.
help.other_computer_w: home laptop transfer take-home sync second computer usb
help.new_address_q: The app moved to a new web address. Where is my work?
help.new_address_a1: Your work is kept by your browser for the address you opened, so a new address starts empty. Nothing is lost: it is still at the old address.
help.new_address_a2: 1. Open the old address. In Settings, **Saving and sync**, press **Take my work with me** and save the file. It holds your grading work and your lessons.
help.new_address_a4: 3. There, in Settings, **Saving and sync**, press **Bring work in** and choose the file.
help.new_address_w: moved address link url website empty gone missing new site domain
help.new_year_q: How do I start a new school year?
help.new_year_a1: 1. In Settings, **Saving and sync**, press **Start a new year**.
help.new_year_a2: 2. Check the two years’ names and what carries over, choose a passphrase and press **Save the file and start the new year**. This year goes into one protected file, and the file is read back and checked before anything is cleared.
help.new_year_a3: Your classes, units and assignment cards stay, each card with its rubric and Quick mark boxes, and dates move on a year. Class lists, papers, scores and comments leave this browser for the file. Units move on a year with the rest.
help.new_year_a4: To look at an old year again, press **Open an archived year** and choose its file. The year you are in is saved to its own file first, so you can switch back.
help.new_year_w: new year next year school year archive rollover reset fresh start august september roster empty
help.go_back_q: I made a mistake. Can I go back to how things were?
help.go_back_a1: Undo (Ctrl Z, or ⌘Z) steps back through the marks on the paper and the scores you gave, one at a time.
help.go_back_a2: Deleting a unit, an assignment or a class shows **Undo** for a few seconds.
help.go_back_a3: For anything bigger, Settings, **Saving and sync**, **Go back in time** lists your work as it was on earlier days. **Look** compares then and now. **Restore this assignment** takes one assignment back and leaves the rest alone.
help.go_back_w: undo restore history lost deleted recover snapshot
help.offline_q: Does it work without the internet?
help.offline_a1: Yes. After the first visit the app is kept on the computer and opens with no connection. Your work never needed one.
help.offline_a2: Settings, **About and updates** can install it as an app with its own window and icon.
help.offline_w: offline wifi install app no connection plane
help.updates_a1: A newer version is fetched quietly, and Settings, **About and updates** says it is ready. Nothing changes until you press **Update now**, which saves your work first.
help.updates_a2: An update never arrives in the middle of marking.
help.updates_w: version new upgrade whats new changed
help.planner_a1: Planning is part of the app now. Each class has a **Course line** of its units and lessons by week, the **Calendar** shows every class by week, by time or by month, and each lesson has its plan, its slides and a slide editor that makes PowerPoint files. The activity bank and the rubric bank are in **Library**.
help.planner_a2: Lessons never hold grading work: student papers, names and scores stay on the grading side.
help.planner_w: lessons units calendar slides plan powerpoint
help.timetable_q: How do I set up my timetable?
help.timetable_a1: In Settings, **Timetable**, type in your classes, when each one meets, and the days school is closed. **Save my setup file** keeps all of it, your slide template included, in one file you can load on another computer.
help.timetable_a2: Home and the Calendar then show the classes you teach each day with the lesson planned for each.
help.timetable_w: schedule periods classes times calendar holidays
help.present_q: How do I present a lesson to the class?
help.present_a1: Open the lesson and press **Present**. Its slides fill the screen; the arrow keys or a clicker move through them. On Home, the class that is next has its own **Present** button.
help.present_a2: While presenting: **A** shows the agenda, **T** starts a timer the class can see, **P** picks a student at random, **G** makes groups, **N** shows your notes, **B** blanks the screen, **W** pops the slides out into their own window for a second screen or projector, and **Esc** finishes.
help.present_a3: The timer takes minutes and seconds. While it runs, its menu adds or takes away 10 seconds or a minute, pauses, and restarts; **+** and **−** add or take away a minute. Tick **Show it big** to put the countdown in the middle of the screen for the back of the room.
help.present_a4: The timer keeps going after you finish or leave full screen: it waits in the corner. Afterwards one line notes where the class got to, and presenting again picks up there.
help.present_w: slideshow full screen projector teach timer countdown seconds agenda clicker second screen monitor window pop out
help.pptx_q: Can I get my slides as a PowerPoint file?
help.pptx_a1: Yes. Open the lesson and choose **Finished PowerPoint** from the menu beside the slides. The file opens in PowerPoint, Keynote and Google Slides.
help.pptx_a2: Slides use a plain white template unless you give it your own: in Settings, **Timetable**, press **Use my school’s template…** and pick a PowerPoint file with a Title Slide and a Title and Content layout.
help.pptx_w: powerpoint pptx template school master export slides keynote google slides download
help.sharelesson_q: How do I move a lesson to another computer or give it to another teacher?
help.sharelesson_a1: Open the lesson and choose **Share lesson file…** from its tools. You get one small file with the slides, notes, pictures, materials and the finished PowerPoint if there is one.
help.sharelesson_a2: On the other computer, press **Import a lesson** in Library, or drop the file on Library. Which classes and days it was on, taught notes and comments for your AI assistant stay behind.
help.sharelesson_w: share send move transfer copy another computer teacher colleague gslesson file import
help.privacy_q: Does student work leave my computer?
help.privacy_a1: No. Papers, names, scores and comments stay in this browser and in the folder you choose. The app has no server and no accounts, and it works with the internet off.
help.privacy_a2: The only things that leave are the files you export yourself.
help.privacy_a3: Once a day, the app at its web address adds one to a public count of how many browsers opened it, so its maker can see whether anyone uses it. Nothing about you, your students or your work goes with it.
help.privacy_w: private data protection gdpr ferpa cloud server secure safe
help.ai_q: Does the app use AI on student work?
help.ai_a1: No. Nothing in the app sends student work to an AI, and scores are only ever given by you.
help.ai_a2: Sharing with an AI assistant, on the Return tab, is optional and off until you use it. It makes a copy with no names in it: each student gets a random code, typed names are covered, and the key stays in your browser.
help.ai_w: artificial intelligence claude chatgpt automatic grading machine
help.remove_q: How do I remove student work from this computer?
help.remove_a1: Settings, **Saving and sync**, **Remove from this computer** clears all student work from this browser once you type REMOVE.
help.remove_a2: It never deletes what is in your linked folder. It says so, stops using the folder and leaves the files for you.
help.remove_w: delete erase clear wipe end of year shared computer
